newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mandela urges global effort to fight Aids.
newsitem.headline: Mandela urges global effort to fight Aids.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela called on Monday for a global battle against Aids saying that the problem was beyond the scope of any individual government.
"The Aids pandemic is getting worse at a rate that makes a collective global effort imperative," Mandela told the World Economic Forum.

Government and top international business leaders, who gather annually at this Swiss mountain resort to debate world problems, greeted the veteran African leader with a standing ovation before he delivered his address.
Mandela said that with 6,000 people each day becoming infected with Aids around the world, there was no doubt that humanity was facing a major challenge.
"Future generations will judge us on the adequacy of our response," he warned.
But in general, the response of individual countries had so far fallen short of what was needed.
Aids was not just a social scourge, it was an economic problem that risked absorbing huge chunks of countries' health budgets and killing people at their productive prime.
Mandela said that Aids would cost South Africa one percent of its whole economic output by the year 2005 and soak up two-thirds of its health budget.
"The severity of the economic impact of the disease is directly related to the fact that most infected persons are in the peak productive and reproductive age groups," he said.

In Africa, the disease was in a sense a legacy of the colonial past. It was the poor, the unschooled, the socially-marginalised -- "those who bear the burden of the colonial legacy, these are the sectors of society which bear the burden of Aids," Mandela said.
